game.name: Loot River
game.short_description: Explore procedurally generated labyrinths in this challenging, narrative-rich roguelike. Master deep combat. Slide blocks of ancient ruins. Defeat bestial abominations. Loot, level up, strategize, fight, die and wake up anew. Unlock the secrets of the Loot River. Immortality is a bittersweet gift.

commentary.label: Tier list Part 1 (2023)
commentary.summary: Loot River is a top-down action roguelike where you fight while also moving the shifting platforms floating on water beneath you. He loves the gimmick, art style and the adventure side (events, bosses, biomes), but finds the moment-to-moment combat repetitive and the game extremely grindy. Early runs repeat the same floor, enemies and spells for hours, and some bosses are cheesable or one-shot you. He calls it underwhelming and feels it could have been really interesting with more time and different design approaches, placing it in a high position of a lower tier.
praise: Unique gimmick of controlling both your character and the water platforms you stand on
Art style and strong adventure vibe
Unique events and bosses are exciting to discover
Skill-heavy; learning to control character plus platform is initially confusing but rewarding
Enjoyed seeing the different bosses and biomes
criticism: Combat portion gets repetitive and boring
One of the grindiest games he has played; unlocks require many runs and gear barely does anything
First floor has few, repeating enemies and few unique spells, so early builds and maps feel identical for hours
Some bosses feel unbalanced: easy to cheese yet able to one-shot you
Slow to get to the fun parts; feels like it should be a puzzle game but does not play like one
unique_points: Controllable floating platforms as the core mechanic, making movement and positioning a puzzle-like layer
Design lesson: a great gimmick needs deeper content variety and faster progression to support it
commentary.quote: I love what they were going for
design_criteria: Gimmick/originality: platform control is a standout concept
Variety: few enemies and spells early, same build repeatedly
Boss design: interesting but unbalanced and cheesable
Difficulty/skill: skill-heavy with a steep, confusing start
Pacing: takes many hours to reach the fun content

community.one_liner: A pixel-art dark-fantasy action roguelite from straka.studio (published with SUPERHOT PRESENTS) where you slide the floating floor tiles of flooded ruins Tetris-style while fighting in stamina-based, souls-flavoured combat.
community.consensus_summary: Loot River landed as a 'fascinating idea, uneven execution' game. Critics were mostly positive (Metacritic 74 from 21 reviews, with scores ranging from 100 down to 40), praising the tile-sliding hook, art and music, while Steam players are Mixed (about 67% positive from roughly 464 reviews) and Metacritic users are lower still at 5.1 (only 13 ratings). The recurring split is between people who click with the soulslike parry/stamina combat and block-shifting puzzle layer, and people who find it clunky, shallow in loot and meta-progression, and buggy. It is a finished 1.0 release (May 2022, Windows only; also appears on Game Pass per a Steam reviewer), but a Steam community thread asks whether it is still being developed, so post-launch support looks quiet. It is now regularly bought for a dollar or a few dollars on sale, and reviewers tend to say it is worth that, not the $25 launch price.
best_things: The tile-sliding mechanic: pushing floating landmasses to bridge gaps, isolate enemies, create chokepoints or escape is praised as a genuinely fresh twist (God is a Geek, Hardcore Gamer, many Steam reviews)
Dark, atmospheric pixel art and an intense soundtrack are the most consistently complimented production elements
Combat, once learned, is described as engaging and well-paced, with parrying and dodge timing rewarding skill
Bosses are said to have distinct mechanics instead of reskinned patterns
Build variety: many weapons, spells and armour pieces plus multiple routes through levels encourage experimentation
An easy/accessibility mode lets players learn the unusual controls and difficulty curve, and modifiers can raise difficulty back up
Short, replayable runs (roughly 5-10 hours to beat, 10-15 for 100%) and a low sale price make it easy to recommend as a change of pace
worst_things: Combat is frequently called clunky, with janky collisions and sloppy hitboxes; one Steam reviewer called it some of the worst combat they had played
Bugs can ruin runs: enemies that lock platform movement can stay in effect after they die, and a boss was knocked outside the arena barrier, forcing restarts
Loot and weapons feel samey (many weapons differ mainly by element and scaling) and meta-progression is very shallow for a game named Loot River
Not much content: several players felt they had seen nearly everything in one or two runs, and Screen Rant scored it 40 saying it feels like an Early Access product
Story and lore are described as boring or forgettable, and endings unfulfilling
Visual clutter and poor visibility during fights make it hard to read the action and spot drops (LEVEL, Metacritic user reviews)
Stamina and parry-heavy design irritates players who wanted fast, fluid roguelike combat
Floating-block mechanic sometimes leaves no route forward, and most weapons are slow, so players feel pushed to abuse parry or die often (Steam negative reviews)
improvements: Fix the soft-locks and bugs (persisting platform locks, bosses leaving arenas, controller remap double-inputs) and keep polishing; players ask whether development is still active
Make loot more interesting and weapons more distinct, with deeper meta-progression
Add more content and gameplay variety, especially mid-run, which GRYOnline.pl and Steam users both allude to
Improve combat readability, hitbox cleanliness and enemy attack/parry timing; some parry-only enemies are said to be nearly impossible to hit
Fix level layouts where the floating mechanic leaves no route forward, and reduce time lost to block-puzzle stalls
Better regional pricing and storefront reach (Steam users ask about Argentina pricing and a GOG release)
unique_things: Tetris-like shifting floor: the map itself is an active weapon and puzzle that you rearrange in real time while fighting
Marketed and reviewed as Dark Souls meets Diablo meets Tetris (The Games Machine, Hardcore Gamer)
You control character movement, attacks and platform pushing at once, which makes controller play close to mandatory
Flooded-ruin setting with procedurally generated labyrinths, a narrative thread and multiple routes
Soulslike stamina/parry combat inside a fast roguelite loop, with easy mode and modifiers to tune difficulty
tedious_or_disliked: Block-shifting puzzles can stall the pace when you are stuck trying to progress, especially when repeated across runs
Stamina management and the delayed parry window frustrate players who find it punishing for any misstep
Unlock/meta loop feels thin, so repeated runs can feel repetitive once the hook wears off
Needing five keys to open gates and other progression gates feel grindy to some players (Steam community thread)
Keyboard and mouse play is widely called awkward, so a controller is effectively required
divisive_points: Is it a souls-like or a roguelite? Players who expected fluid roguelike combat bounced off; those expecting deliberate soulslike combat loved it
Difficulty and easy mode: some say easy mode is essential to learn it, others say hard mode is only frustrating, not rewarding
Length and price: fine at $1-4 on sale, but many say too little content at the $20-25 launch price
Critics scored it far higher (74 average) than Metacritic users (5.1, just 13 ratings) and Steam players (about 67% positive)
community.reception_notes: Launched May 3, 2022 on Steam (Windows, $24.99) with SUPERHOT PRESENTS as co-publisher; critics were generally warm on the concept while Steam settled at Mixed and Metacritic user score ended at 5.1. Metacritic's 74 comes from 21 critics; user reviews there cite clunky combat, poor visibility, repetitive puzzles and an unfinished feel. Steam reviews continue to arrive years later (through 2026), often praising it as a cheap, short, flawed-but-interesting pick from a first-time studio, and commonly noting it was picked up for about $1-4 on sale or via Game Pass. The Steam discussion board shows reports of many bugs, a controller-remap double-input bug, requests for a GOG release and regional pricing, and a thread asking whether the game is still actively developed. One Steam reviewer says expectations were set wrongly by a souls-focused YouTuber recommendation and that the game is a shallow-progression roguelite, not a souls-like. OpenCritic score could not be retrieved: web search budget was exhausted and the direct OpenCritic URL guesses did not resolve, so it is left null. Reddit and several outlet URLs (PC Gamer, Screen Rant, Game Informer, IGN) were blocked or 404.
